name: Oye Kake
description: Oye Kake – The Soul of Amritsar Food. Built on tradition, love, and warm hospitality, it brings the comforting and rich flavours of Punjab to life. The dishes are inspired by old cooking practices, fresh ingredients, and the balance of being both tasty and healthy. Oye Kake celebrates the lively and generous Punjabi spirit, offering every guest a memorable experience of service (seva), peace (sukoon) and flavour (swaad).

featured_reviews.review_text:
Good service, okay ambience, and overall average food experience.

We tried a few dishes:
Lasooni chaap – 3/5. I’ve had better chaap before; this one wasn’t very soft and leaned slightly on the sweeter side, which didn’t work for me.

Papdi paneer cheese shot – 1/5. This was recommended by the staff but turned out to be quite disappointing. It was deep-fried yet soggy instead of crispy, which ruined the texture completely.

Pyaaz and garlic kulcha – 4/5. This was the highlight of the meal. The stuffing was flavorful, and it tasted great. It comes with chole, which complemented it well.

Overall, an okay experience—not bad, but not something I’d specifically go back for.

featured_reviews.name: Santosh Mane
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently enjoyed a wonderful family dinner at this gem in Ghatkopar. 🍴 The food was flavorful and thoughtfully prepared based on regional tastes, pleasing both kids and adults alike.

Hospitality stood out throughout making everyone feel welcome 🤝.

Having such a special food stop offering all key maharastrian recipes in Ghatkopar and proximity is a big plus. We loved Tambada/pandhara rassa, Solkadhi, and delicious non-veg khandeshi dishes 😋.

Highly recommend this restaurant in Ghatkopar for a family outing. Great food, excellent service, genuine hospitality, and a convenient location—perfect for creating lasting memories.
We’ll be definitely visiting again!

featured_reviews.name: Pranay Panchal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I honestly don’t understand the hype around Biryani By Kilo’s Hyderabadi biryani. Ordered it expecting that rich, aromatic, authentic experience—but what I got was just disappointing.

First off, the rice and meat felt completely disconnected. A good Hyderabadi biryani should have that deep infusion of flavors where every bite hits—but here it tasted like the masala never really seeped in. The chicken was just okay, nothing juicy or tender enough to stand out.

And the spice balance? Either bland in parts or randomly overpowering in others. It lacked that signature warmth and complexity you expect. The aroma was there when I opened the pot, but the taste just didn’t live up to it.

For the price they charge, this felt more like a watered-down version of what Hyderabadi biryani is supposed to be. Definitely not worth the premium tag.

Really expected better—this one missed the mark.

featured_reviews.name: Sunny Gurnani
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently tried a meal from Biryani by kilo which has been on my wishlist from quite sometime. With their good options it might get difficult to zero down on your order hence I tried something flavorful which is chicken ghee roast that had soft chicken pieces cooked in ghee roast style. It had some excess gravy and oil but tasted really amazing. From the biryani section I picked chicken Lucknowi biryani which was half cooked outside and half inside the pot. What i loved the most other than they serving biryani in clay pot Handi is that they also send you another clay pot vessel called Aanch which has candles in it so even if you are ordering during this lockdown times when you will eat later all you have to do is put the candles on and keep it for 5 to 8mins to get the freshness back along with hot serving. The biryani was succulent with not alot of gravy but very little keeping your rice dry and non greasy but the Lucknowi flavors are truly mesmerizing. Next I had firni from dessert which came in hot in a handi again. It tasted about good.

All in all a great expertise wanting me to try more of their biryani soon again

featured_reviews.name: Monish Chandan
featured_reviews.review_text:
We Indians eat our meal in sumptuous way. BBK aptly serves it the same way. The concept of Kilo is when you have big party or get together then enjoy the cuisine in a grand way. What sets BBK apart is their  traditional way cooking and authentic biryani taste.

Hyderabadi Paneer Biryani ; the Indian spices having BBK flavors blends well with the fresh paneer & veggies. Loved the texture and the taste was so delicious 😋.
Vegetarian lovers gonna love this

Dal nizami; the twist in normal dal makhani is amazing here.  If you're dal makhani lover then definitely try this nizami one.

Our meal ended with Double ka meetha; It's more like a shahi tukda, It was so yummy

And rightly said There's always a reason to celebrate to indulge in BBK.

featured_reviews.name: Bhooshan Shetty
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently got a chance to try this place out and was really impressed. Just like the name suggests biryani by kilo serves authentic biryani in large quantities in their pot shaped container which is super amazing.
And the icing on the cake would be the smaller container filled with candles which is sent by them to heat up your biryani to give that extra smoky flavour to it. Authentic Dum Biryani it is. Missing your usual dinning experience, well their packing would make sure you don't.

Moving over to the taste, I had murgh Hyderabadi biryani which had a really good flavour to it. The spices were moderate and wasn't overpowering my taste buds. The chicken pieces were tender and succulent as well.

I also tried their chicken seekh kebab which was good as well it had a mild flavour to it a great partner to have with your biryani is what I would say.

Finally for dessert I had their gulab jamun with rabri and ohh boy I was impressed with it. It is a must try, a perfect ending to a perfect meal. Must Try!!

Loved the overall experience, a great place to order for some really authentic biryani and also their large servings make it a perfect place for large gatherings. Though I won't recommend large gatherings haha.
Really looking forward to ordering from this place again.

This goes well, succulent and soft piece of paneer easy pricked with finger which absorb all the flavours from the gravy. The gravy was onion-tomato based, slightly thick with ginger julienne aromatic with kewra water and was mellow in flavour slightly sweet from the onions and best goes with Ulte Tawa ka Paratha. The plus point is the taste and quantity of the gravy which can be sharable between 4-5peoples. Highly recommended for this.

Ulte Tawa ka Paratha: Without any doubt, I ordered for this and  good, paratha was warm till it arrives at place. Thin, soft and easily break within the fingers and absorb all the gravy when it was dunk on it. The size is bigger comparing to those days which is too good. Recommended to have this here.

Hyderabad Chicken Dum Biryani: No second thought on this. The long grain basmati rice cooked to perfection in succulent pieces of chicken coated well in marination taste medium spicy but with mild aromatic flavour of spices, ghee and slight sweetness from the fried onions. The biryani certainly had absorbed the flavours of ghee even it turn aromatic to Chicken. This is the sort of Biryani which is completed in itself and enjoyable but to accompaniment it serves with Mirchi ka Saalan which slightly disappointed because of raw smell of peanuts and big size of red chillies taste need to improvise here. Highly recommended if you love your Biryani mellow and mild spicy.

Skipped the dessert this time.

Packaging was done too good and no spillage at all, delivery was done on time prior to given time.

For mains, we tried the Pink Lady Mee (Chicken). It was flavourful, vibrant, and nicely balanced.

Dessert was a pleasant surprise with the Shrikhand Crème Brûlée, blending classic Indian flavours with a modern twist — a perfect end to the meal.

Overall, Curry’s & Cocktails offers a lovely dining experience with good food, creative drinks, and versatile spaces to suit every mood — from relaxed family dinners to high-energy nights with music. Definitely worth a visit if you’re in or around Ghatkopar.

I visited Copper Chimney at R City Mall, Ghatkopar, and the experience beautifully reflected their legendary 53-year legacy. Celebrating their 53rd Anniversary, they are offering an amazing 53% off on their iconic Originals Since 1972 and Autograph Dishes, making the visit even more special.

We began with their signature Kadak Roomali with Black Chana Dip, followed by refreshing mocktails like Dalchini Sherbet, Spice Punch, Mumbai Mastani and Anar Kali each one perfectly crafted.

In starters, the original signature Achari Chicken Tikka and Paneer Tikka were smoky, soft, and full of bold flavours. For mains, the Rogan Josh (Lamb) stood out with its deep, aromatic Kashmiri curry notes, and the Palak Goolar Kofta impressed with its creamy almond-cashew gravy and rich spinach–mawa–fig stuffing.

The breads Punjabi Onion & Mirch Roti, Garlic Naan, and Butter Lachcha Paratha paired perfectly with both veg and non-veg curries.

We ended our meal with their signature dessert Muzaffar, thick Lucknowi rabdi topped with roasted vermicelli, and a soft, creamy Rasmalai the perfect sweet finish.

From flavours to service to legacy, Copper Chimney truly lives up to being a classic since 1972. A must-visit for anyone who appreciates authentic North Indian cuisine, timeless recipes, and warm hospitality. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Tulsi Tanna
featured_reviews.review_text:
Have you been mocked at when ordering a VEGETARIAN Biryani?
I have been, a several times. I was told, there is no such thing as VEG Biryani, it's just Veg Pulao masked under the name of Biryani.

It was after experiencing The Biryani Kahani, that I realised what had I been missing the whole time!

Let me explain by telling you what I ordered:

☑️ Subz Shami Kebab
Kebab is synonym for a minced meat starter. But the soft & aromatic vegetable kebab gave a different meaning to kebabs. It is served with delicious mint chutney to balance the flavours.

☑️ Pahadi Paneer Tikka
Soft cottage cheese marinated in refreshing flavours of mint, chilly, garlic & coriander. I found the flavour of garlic to be overpowering in this otherwise perfect starter.

☑️ Dum Aloo Biryani
I got lost in the smoked flavours of baby potatoes marinated with spices & long and whole Basmati rice. Saffron adds to the richness and the earthen pot to the authenticity. Alongside came cumin-curd raita and salad.

❤️ Kesariya Phirni
Let me introduce you to the highlight of the meal - Kesariya Phirni. I'm not a fan of kheer or phirni but this pot of magic enchanted me with its richness of saffron, cardamom & almond and creaminess of rice & milk. Perfect dessert for all.
#MustHave

🎁Packaging
I got blown away when I saw the packaging of the Biryani. It came packed in an earthen pot sealed with dough. The best part was the Angithi that came along. Angithi is an earthen bowl with a tea light that helps heat up the Biryani Handi.

🌰 NUTSHELL REVIEW
If you are looking for authentic Moghul flavours, order from The Biryani Kahani, where they offer not just food but a wholesome experience through their delivery kitchen.

Visited this place with my friends after hearing a lot about it, and it truly lived up to the expectations. We had a fantastic experience—both the food and the overall vibe were excellent.

We ordered Bombil fry as a starter, along with Prawns Thali and Surmai Thali. Every single dish was 10/10. Personally, whenever I try a new place for fish, I judge it by the taste of the Bombil fry—and this one was outstanding. It was extremely fresh, perfectly crispy, and the masala was well balanced and nicely blended.

The same quality and freshness reflected in the Surmai and Prawns thali—authentic taste and very satisfying portions.

On the owner’s suggestion, we also tried their Mutton Thali for a change, and it was surprisingly excellent. The mutton was fresh, tender, and full of flavour, which is rare to find these days.

If you’re a seafood lover, this place is a must-visit. Highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy quality fish with great taste and vibes.

customer_updates.name: Ajay Kodeesvaran
customer_updates.text:
If you’re in Ghatkopar and craving authentic South Indian food, Bharat Cafe is an absolute must-visit!
I’ve been here multiple times, and the consistency in taste and quality is impressive. Their Idli is incredibly soft, the Medu Vada perfectly crisp, and the Sambar has that classic balanced flavour – not overly spicy, just comforting and homely. The coconut chutney tastes fresh every single time, which is rare these days.
One thing I truly appreciate is how quickly they serve despite the heavy crowd. The place is usually buzzing, yet the staff manages orders efficiently without compromising service. It has that old-school Mumbai charm – simple seating, no frills, but full of flavour.
Highly recommend: ✔️ Ghee Roast Dosa
✔️ Filter Coffee (strong and aromatic)
✔️ Upma (surprisingly flavourful and light)
Pricing is very reasonable for the portion size and quality. Whether it’s a quick breakfast stop or an evening snack craving, Bharat Cafe never disappoints.

At ₹70, the idli itself felt poorly prepared, and the sambar had a strange sharp taste, almost acidic, as if too much soda had been added. Pricing would still be acceptable if the quality matched, but that simply was not the case here. Expensive food is understandable, disappointing food at premium prices is not.

Good spot for chai and hanging out, but if you care about food quality and value, I would avoid coming here for dinner.

Good food, but the value for money really hurts – Bhagat Tarachand, Ghatkopar East

As a food blogger who eats out across Mumbai, I finally stopped by Bhagat Tarachand, Ghatkopar East after hearing so much about their consistent North Indian and Sindhi-style food. The taste did live up to the reputation – but the pricing and portion size left me honestly disappointed, hence this 3-star review.

Ambience & First Impressions

The outlet has a clean, family-restaurant vibe – bright lighting, compact seating and a steady flow of diners through the evening. It’s clearly a popular pure veg restaurant in Ghatkopar East for families and big groups, and service is quick and efficient even during peak hours.

You get that old-school Bhagat Tarachand feel – steel plates, homely gravies and attentive servers – but with the pricing and polish of a modern air-conditioned dine-in.

Food: Tasty, Comforting, Old-School Flavours

No complaints on the flavour front. The sabzis, phulkas and accompaniments all tasted homely and well-balanced. The greens we ordered (a saag / leafy veggie preparation with potatoes) was delicious – properly spiced, loaded with fresh methi/palak, and cooked in that classic, slightly rustic BT style.

Overall, this is the kind of food that pairs beautifully with hot phulkas, chaas and a relaxed family dinner. If you’re searching for North Indian veg food in Ghatkopar East, Bhagat Tarachand still knows how to deliver on taste.

The Big Let-down: ₹450 for a Limited Veg Thali

Where the experience really dipped for me was the pricing of the veg thali.
•	₹450 for a veg thali (limited, no refills)
•	Quantity felt modest – especially the sabzis and dal portions
•	For this price point, you naturally expect either generous servings or at least unlimited refills on core items (dal, sabzi, phulka/rice)

Unfortunately, this was a strictly limited thali, and the amount of food on the plate simply didn’t feel justified for ₹450 – especially when you compare it with other popular thali restaurants in Ghatkopar and across Mumbai that offer similar or better portions, often with refills, at a lower or comparable price.

As a diner, you walk out feeling that the value-for-money equation is off, even though your taste buds are happy.

Service

Service was polite and fairly quick – staff is used to handling heavy crowds and multiple thali orders at once. Water, accompaniments and roti service were prompt, and the servers are courteous and attentive without hovering.

No complaints on that front – the issue here is purely the pricing vs quantity, not the people or their hospitality.

Verdict: Worth It for Taste Once in a While, Not for Regular Visits

To sum it up:

Pros
•	Flavourful, satisfying vegetarian food
•	Classic Bhagat Tarachand style gravies and greens
•	Clean, family-friendly ambience in Ghatkopar East
•	Quick and polite service

Cons
•	₹450 for a limited veg thali feels exorbitant
•	Portion size does not justify the price
•	Overall experience feels expensive for what’s on the plate

If you’re a Bhagat Tarachand loyalist, you’ll enjoy the familiar taste and may not mind paying a premium once in a while. But as a value-conscious food lover exploring restaurants in Ghatkopar, I’d say come here knowing that you’re paying more for the brand and nostalgia than for sheer quantity.

Overall rating: 3/5 – tasty food, but the high price for a limited thali stops this from being a place I’d frequent regularly.

I rarely write reviews, but our experience at Bhagat Tarachand (Ghatkopar) was deeply disappointing and upsetting — especially because I visited with my mother, expecting a pleasant meal. From the moment we entered, we were made to sit right next to the washroom, despite other tables being available. Even more frustrating, people who arrived after us not only received the exact same order before us, but the attentiveness and service they received was noticeably different. The raita we were served was too tangy, so we politely requested a little sugar. It took the waiter 10 minutes just to bring that — something that should have taken seconds. Asking for extra rotis was another struggle. The staff showed visible reluctance and even attitude when we requested them, and again, they were brought very late. Throughout the meal, we felt neglected — as if our presence was an inconvenience and we weren’t paying customers. Every item we ordered was delayed or treated dismissively. The service we received made us feel like we were eating there for free. What made it worse was the clear difference in how we were treated compared to others. As both of us were wearing abaya's , it was hard to ignore the stark contrast in behavior and courtesy extended to us versus other diners. The sense of bias in the service was not just disappointing — it was hurtful. Restaurants should treat every customer with basic respect, regardless of appearance or attire. Sadly, that standard was not met here.

I hope the management takes this feedback seriously. No one should be made to feel unwelcome at a place meant for hospitality.
